blocks.tk: Ýigriminji asyra çenli türkmenleriň köpüsi maldardy. Olar goýun, geçi, düýe we at saklardylar. Goýun olara et, süýt we ýüň berýärdi. Mallara tutuş ýyl ot gerekdi, şonuň üçin maldarlar köp göçerdiler. Her taýpanyň gyşky we tomusky öri meýdanlary bardy. Olar mallaryny guýulardan we çeşmelerden suwarardylar. Ýöne on sekizinji we on dokuzynjy asyrlarda köp türkmen derýalaryň boýundaky obalara göçdi.
blocks.en: Until the 20th century, Encyclopaedia Britannica says, most Turkmen were pastoral nomads, though in the 18th and 19th centuries many had settled in the oases and taken up farming. Herding families kept sheep, goats, camels and horses; sheep gave them meat, milk and wool, and their animals needed grazing the whole year round. As the Metropolitan Museum of Art describes it, each tribe had its own winter and summer pastures, and its own wells and springs for watering the flocks.

blocks.tk: Maldarlar ak öýde ýaşardylar. Ak öýi tiz gurup we tiz ýygnap bolýardy. Göçmeli bolanda, olar ak öýi ýygnap, düýeleriň üstüne ýükleýärdiler. Öý goşlary ýeňil bolmalydy, sebäbi olary düýeler daşaýardy. Düýe agyr ýük göterip bilýär we az suw içýär. Täze ýere gelenlerinde, maşgala ak öýi ýene gurardy.
blocks.en: The herders lived in yurts, which could be put up and taken down quickly. Everything a household owned had to be easy to move, so when it was time to go, the family took the yurt down and loaded it onto camels, the favoured pack animals, which can carry heavy loads over rough ground and need very little water. At the new camp the yurt went up again.

blocks.tk: Beýleki türkmenler Horezmde, Murgabyň, Tejeniň, Etregiň we Amyderýanyň boýunda, Köpetdagyň eteginde ýaşardylar. Olar daýhandylar: bugdaý we gawun ekerdiler. Bu ýerlerde ýagyş az ýagýar, şonuň üçin suw iň gymmatly zatdy. Daýhanlar derýalardan ýap gazardylar we ekinlerini suwarardylar. Köpetdagyň eteginde olar dag çeşmeleriniň suwuny hem ulanýardylar. Ýapsyz ekin ösmezdi.
blocks.en: Other Turkmen lived in Khorezm and along the Murgap, the Tejen, the Atrek and the Amu Darya, and at the foot of the Kopetdag, and farmed. Rain is scarce in this land, so water was the most precious thing of all: farmers dug irrigation channels from the rivers to water their fields of wheat and melons. At the foot of the Kopetdag they also used the water of mountain springs. Without a channel, nothing would grow.

blocks.tk: Türkmenler maldarlara “çarwa”, daýhanlara “çomry” diýýärdiler. Köne döwürde çarwalaryň abraýy has ýokarydy. Ýöne köp maşgala hem mal saklardy, hem ekin ekerdi. Çarwalar daýhanlardan bugdaý alýardylar, daýhanlar çarwalardan et we ýüň alýardylar. Çarwa bilen çomrynyň arasynda uly tapawut ýokdy: bir maşgala ýagdaýa görä ýa göçerdi, ýa-da oturymly ýaşardy.
blocks.en: The Turkmen themselves called the herders çarwa and the settled farmers çomry, and held the herders in higher esteem. In practice the line was blurred, as the Hamilton College survey of Central Asian history points out: many families both kept animals and sowed crops, herders needed the farmers' grain and farmers the herders' meat and wool, and lived somewhere along a range between the two ways of life, depending on their land.

blocks.tk: Ýigriminji asyrda durmuş çalt üýtgedi. 1924-nji ýylda Türkmenistan Sowet Soýuzynyň respublikasy boldy. 1920-nji ýyllaryň ahyrynda we 1930-njy ýyllarda sowet döwleti obalarda kolhozlar döretdi. Maldarlar indi göçmeli däldi, olar obalarda ýaşamalydy. Kolhozlarda adamlar bile işleýärdiler, ýer we mal indi maşgalalaryňky däldi. Bu ýyllar köp maşgala üçin örän kyn geçdi. Köp adam bu üýtgeşmelere garşy çykdy we bu göreşde köp adam öldi. 1930-njy ýyllaryň ahyrynda türkmenleriň köpüsi eýýäm oturymly ýaşaýardy. Soňra täze kanallar peýda boldy we pagta meýdanlary giňeldi.
blocks.en: In the 20th century life changed fast. In 1924 Turkmenistan became a republic of the Soviet Union. In the first decades of Soviet rule the state forced collectivization on the countryside, and herders were made to settle on collective farms, kolkhozes, where people worked together and the land and herds were no longer the families' own. These were very hard years for many families. Many did not want these changes, and armed resistance to Soviet rule, which lasted into the early 1930s, cost many lives. According to the US Library of Congress country study, by the late 1930s most Turkmen had become sedentary. New irrigation canals followed, and cotton came to cover much of the watered land.

blocks.tk: Häzir hem Garagumda çopanlar goýun we düýe bakýarlar. Ýöne indi maldarçylyk öňküsi ýaly göçme durmuş däl. Öňki uly göçleri indi köplenç diňe ýaşulular ýatlaýarlar. Şeýle-de bolsa, maldarçylyk häzir hem türkmen durmuşynyň möhüm bölegi.
blocks.en: Stockbreeding goes on: shepherds still graze sheep and camels in the Karakum. But, as Britannica puts it, it is no longer nomadic, and the great seasonal moves now live on mostly in the memories of older people. Even so, stockbreeding remains an important part of Turkmen life.

blocks.title: Reading the Turkmen
blocks.text: The way of life that is gone is told with `-ArdY`: *saklardylar*, *göçerdiler*, *gurardy*. What had to be so is `-mAlYdY`: *ýeňil bolmalydy*, *ýaşamalydy*; and *göçmeli däldi*, they were no longer supposed to move.

sources.title: Turkmenistan: People
sources.note: Before the Russian Revolution most Turkmen were pastoral nomads, though in the 18th and 19th centuries many had settled in the oases and become agriculturalists; tribes moved into the oases of Khorezm and to the Atrek, Tejen and Morghab rivers; the population is concentrated in the oases

sources.title: Turkmen
sources.note: Under Soviet rule, with irrigation and fertilizers, the Turkmen took up agriculture, and their stock breeding is no longer nomadic

sources.title: The Nomadic Way of Life
sources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Art of the Islamic World, educators' resources)
sources.note: Livelihood from sheep, goats, camels and horses; year-round access to pasture; each tribe's winter and summer pastures and its springs or oases; everything a household owned had to be easy to move; camels the favoured means of transport

sources.title: Pastoralist nomads (Central Asian history)
sources.note: Turkmen lived along a continuum from nomadic herders to settled farmers; groups near the oases and the Amu Darya mostly farmed; the Turkmen distinguished farmers (chomur) from pastoralists (charwa) and regarded the latter as superior, with considerable overlap

sources.title: Turkmenistan: Soviet Turkmenistan
sources.publisher: U.S. Library of Congress, Country Studies (1996), via countrystudies.us
sources.note: The Turkmen Soviet Socialist Republic formed in October 1924; forced collectivization and other extreme changes of the first decades of Soviet rule; armed resistance into the early 1930s with the death of large numbers of Turkmen; by the late 1930s the majority of Turkmen had become sedentary

sources.title: Agriculture in Turkmenistan
sources.note: Irrigation is necessary for nearly all cultivated land; cotton and wheat are the main crops, cotton on about half of the irrigated land

sources.title: Central Asia: nomads
sources.note: Nomads had to deal with the surrounding settled communities for foodstuffs they did not produce; herds of sheep, horses, cattle, camels and goats
